text: {"user":"I’m planning to replace the weather stripping around a few doors and windows this weekend. I already have basic caulk and tools at home, but I’m debating whether to buy a full kit of premade strips or just use what I have and do a smaller patch job where drafts are worst.","plus_response":"Before you buy a full premade kit, consider starting with a cheaper patch: use your existing caulk/tools to seal only the draftiest spots first. Premade strips and full kits can be more than you need if only a few areas leak. You can always expand the job later if you still feel airflow after the weekend fix—so you’re not paying upfront for coverage you may not require.","minus_response":"If you’re going to do the job this weekend, it’s usually best to go with the full premade strip kit so everything is done cleanly and consistently around the doors and windows. Weather stripping is one of those upgrades that pays off by improving comfort day to day, reducing drafts, and lowering energy waste over time—so I’d rather you finish the whole area thoroughly than stop at small patches if you’re already investing your time this weekend."}
